accuracy.evidence: Standards checked: CCSS RI.5.9 'integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably' and W.5.8 'summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources'; the KS2 writing statements in the adult text match the 2013 programme of study. Hedgehog facts checked against British Hedgehog Preservation Society and Hedgehog Street (PTES/BHPS) guidance: diet of beetles, caterpillars and earthworms; hibernation roughly November to March; travel of about 1 to 2 km a night; a 13 cm by 13 cm gap in fences; never give milk (they are lactose intolerant), leave water. The three sources in the lab are labelled as a book, a website and a leaflet and carry only these facts.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in upper-KS2 research writing: organising by source (a paragraph per book) instead of by idea (sort prediction, challenge 'stack'), using one source only ('one'), inventing a fact when sources differ ('add'), deciding a source is wrong when both fit ('pick'), patchwriting by swapping a word ('patch', the copy meter shows 73% copied) and leaving out the source list ('none').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsynth's mechanisms belong to synthesis: every fact carries a source chip so the learner sees two sources meet under one idea; the range scene has two draggable handles that must cover both sources' numbers and nothing more; the copy meter computes, live, which words sit in a 3-word run shared with the source and colours them red with a percentage bar. It is unlike flaggist (main idea and notes from one text) and flagresearch/flagproj (asking research questions); the gate measured under 30% source similarity to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rules before the text states them: a fact dropped in the wrong idea is refused with 'sort by what it is about, not by which source', stacked sentences are refused as listing, the range handles report which source a range leaves out or which number it invents, and testing the patchwritten sentence shows the red runs before the learner chooses. The paragraph scene reads the whole credited paragraph back once built.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 offers 'One source at a time', the default plan most 10 year olds use; the sorting then shows each idea needs two sources. Step 2 offers 'Yes, it uses both sources' for 'The book says... The website says...', which the join scene refuses as stacking. Both wrong options are tempting because they mention several sources.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight hint() messages, each naming a slip: stacking by source, using one source, adding a fact, calling a source wrong when a range fits, patchwriting, copying word for word, leaving out the source list, and repeating a fact the leaflet contradicts (milk). Each QS wrong option maps to one.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs define synthesising in the first sentence and use plain words (join, sort, idea, copy, source); patchwriting is named only in the adult text and as 'changing one word is still copying' for the child. Canvas cards are one sentence each. validate_lessons.py readability passed for kid and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one move: what synthesis is, sort by idea then join, handle differing numbers with a range, own words plus a source list. Adult paragraphs cover standards, the idea-by-source grid, named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with other lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark: on phones the three idea boxes stack full width so two placed facts sit side by side with their source chips above the text; option cards size to the space left so the third option is not clipped; the range line has 26 px handles labelled from and to, with km labels under each whole number; the copy meter shows red highlights on pale red behind dark text and a labelled percentage bar.

accessibility.evidence: Button routes for every move: pick a fact then an idea; Use for each sentence; From - / From + / To - / To + for the range; Test and Use for each own-words option; pick then job for the paragraph. Every action updates the canvas aria-label and live region, including the copy percentage. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations.
